# TASK

Summarise this conversation, following the guidelines below.


# CONTEXT

- The user, labelled “YOU”, has recorded the conversation with “THEM”. 
- The user requires a clear, very concise, and useful summary.
- The summary will be ingested into a organisational knowledge graph and linked to relevant entities and topics.


# GUIDE

- Use BLUF, STE-ASD100, and best practices for note taking
- Prioritise what the user ("YOU") learned from THEM.
- Keep what the user said brief, only as context.
- If you know speaker names, insert them for “THEM”
- Use very short bullets
- Do NOT use "- **label**: description"
- Return Markdown


# STRUCTURE

By default, use the following structure:


## BLUF

1 short paragraph with 1-2 short sentences


## Key points

- a limited number of very concise bullet points
- capture what the user(!) needs to take away from the conversation


### topic 1

- you can use "###" subsections to group related points
- ONLY use this if multiple different AND important topics are discussed


## Narrative

- bullet points outlining the narrative flow of how the conversation developed


## Follow-up (if any) 

- [ ] Action items or next steps agreed upon

# TASK

# GUIDE

- Prioritise what the user ("YOU") learned from THEM.

# STRUCTURE

## BLUF

1-2 short sentences stating the outcome or current status.

## Decisions

- Very short bullets stating what was agreed
- If no decision was made, say so briefly

## Follow-up (if any)

- [ ] Action items or next steps agreed upon, with names and dates when stated

## Open questions (if any)

- Unresolved points that need a decision
detailed: Write a detailed chronological summary that preserves important reasoning, decisions, action items, risks, disagreements, and open questions without inventing facts.
